title: Given a Scenario, Use the Appropriate Tool or Protocol to Solve Networking Issues

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Troubleshooting tools answer different questions. The exam gives you a symptom and expects the tool or command that produces the most direct evidence.
sections.callout: TEST REACHABILITY → TRACE PATH → CHECK NAME RESOLUTION → INSPECT TRAFFIC → INSPECT HOST → DISCOVER NETWORK → TEST PHYSICAL → INSPECT DEVICE

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Choose the narrowest tool that directly answers the question in the scenario.
bullets: Where does the path stop? → traceroute/tracert
What does DNS return? → nslookup or dig
What is inside the traffic? → Protocol analyzer or tcpdump
Which ports are listening locally? → netstat
Which systems and services exist? → Nmap
Where does this cable go? → Toner

sections.title: Protocol Analyzer
paragraphs: A protocol analyzer captures and decodes network traffic so you can inspect headers, conversations, retransmissions, handshakes, errors, and application behavior. It is the broad analysis category; tcpdump is a command-line capture tool.
sections.callout: Need packet-level proof? Capture the traffic.

entries.title: ping
paragraphs: Tests basic IP reachability and round-trip response using ICMP.
entries.memoryHook: Can I reach it?

entries.title: traceroute / tracert
paragraphs: Shows the hop-by-hop path toward a destination and helps locate where delay or failure begins.
entries.memoryHook: Where does the path stop?

entries.title: nslookup
paragraphs: Queries DNS and is widely available for basic name-resolution testing.
entries.memoryHook: What address does this name resolve to?

entries.title: tcpdump
paragraphs: Captures and filters packets from the command line.
entries.memoryHook: Packet capture in a terminal.

entries.title: dig
paragraphs: Performs detailed DNS queries and exposes record and response information.
entries.memoryHook: Detailed DNS investigation.

entries.title: netstat
paragraphs: Displays local network connections, listening ports, statistics, and—in some implementations—routing information.
entries.memoryHook: What is this host listening to or connected with?

entries.title: ip / ifconfig / ipconfig
paragraphs: Displays or manages host interface and IP configuration. The exact command depends on the operating system.
entries.memoryHook: What is this host's network configuration?

entries.title: arp
paragraphs: Displays or manages the host's ARP cache, which maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses on the local network.
entries.memoryHook: What MAC does this host associate with that local IP?

entries.title: Nmap
paragraphs: Discovers hosts, open ports, and services across a network.
entries.memoryHook: Scan the network, not just the local host.

entries.title: LLDP / CDP
paragraphs: Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) and Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) reveal directly connected network neighbors and their advertised identity, port, and capabilities.
entries.memoryHook: Who is connected next door?

entries.title: Speed Tester
paragraphs: Measures achieved transfer rate and often latency to assess end-user performance.
entries.memoryHook: How fast is the connection in practice?

entries.title: Toner
paragraphs: Places a detectable tone on copper cabling so a probe can trace or identify the correct cable.
entries.memoryHook: Find where the cable goes.

entries.title: Cable Tester
paragraphs: Checks continuity, pinout, opens, shorts, crossed pairs, and other wiring faults.
entries.memoryHook: Prove whether the cable is wired correctly.

entries.title: Network Tap
paragraphs: Provides a dedicated observation point that copies traffic for monitoring or packet capture.
entries.memoryHook: Get traffic to the analyzer.

entries.title: Wi-Fi Analyzer
paragraphs: Measures wireless channels, signal strength, nearby networks, utilization, and interference patterns.
entries.memoryHook: See the radio environment.

entries.title: Visual Fault Locator
paragraphs: Injects visible light into fiber to reveal breaks, severe bends, and faulty connectors over short distances.
entries.memoryHook: Visible light exposes a fiber fault.

entries.title: show mac-address-table
paragraphs: Displays the switch's learned mapping of MAC addresses to interfaces and VLANs.
entries.memoryHook: Where did the switch learn this MAC?

entries.title: show route
paragraphs: Displays known destination networks, next hops, and route selection information.
entries.memoryHook: How will the device reach that network?

entries.title: show interface
paragraphs: Displays link state, speed, duplex, counters, errors, and interface details.
entries.memoryHook: What is happening on this port?

entries.title: show config
paragraphs: Displays the device configuration so intended settings can be reviewed or compared.
entries.memoryHook: How is the device configured?

entries.title: show arp
paragraphs: Displays the network device's IP-to-MAC neighbor mappings.
entries.memoryHook: Which MAC corresponds to this local IP?

entries.title: show vlan
paragraphs: Displays VLANs and port membership.
entries.memoryHook: Which logical segment owns this port?

entries.title: show power
paragraphs: Displays power supply or PoE use, availability, and delivery information.
entries.memoryHook: Is power available and being delivered?

sections.title: Tool Selection Workflow
bullets: Start with host configuration: ip, ifconfig, or ipconfig
Test a nearby and then remote address: ping
Trace a failing route: traceroute or tracert
Test the name service directly: nslookup or dig
Discover remote hosts and services: Nmap
Capture traffic: tcpdump or a protocol analyzer
Trace and test physical media: toner, cable tester, or visual fault locator
Confirm device forwarding and configuration: show commands

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Short fiber fault → Visual fault locator

entries.title: ping vs. traceroute
paragraphs: ping tests reachability; traceroute/tracert reveals the path and failure point.

entries.title: nslookup vs. dig
paragraphs: Both query DNS; dig generally exposes more detailed record and response data.

entries.title: Protocol Analyzer vs. tcpdump
paragraphs: Protocol analyzer is the analysis category; tcpdump is a command-line capture utility.

entries.title: netstat vs. Nmap
paragraphs: netstat inspects the local host's connections and listeners; Nmap scans hosts and services on the network.

entries.title: arp vs. show arp
paragraphs: arp examines a host cache; show arp examines the table on a networking device.

entries.title: Toner vs. Cable Tester
paragraphs: A toner traces and identifies a cable; a cable tester validates wiring and continuity.

entries.title: Tap vs. Protocol Analyzer
paragraphs: A tap supplies a copy of traffic; an analyzer captures and interprets it.

entries.title: Wi-Fi Analyzer vs. Speed Tester
paragraphs: A Wi-Fi analyzer examines RF conditions; a speed tester measures achieved network performance.

entries.title: show mac-address-table vs. show arp
paragraphs: The MAC table maps MACs to switch ports; ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses.

entries.title: show interface vs. show config
paragraphs: show interface examines operational port details; show config examines configured settings.

entries.title: show vlan vs. show mac-address-table
paragraphs: show vlan reveals VLAN membership; show mac-address-table reveals learned device locations.

entries.title: show power vs. show interface
paragraphs: show power focuses on power/PoE capacity and use; show interface focuses on link operation and counters.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: REACH → TRACE → RESOLVE → CAPTURE → INSPECT → DISCOVER → TEST → VERIFY
